title: How Topocode previews a committed story
summary: Follow the factual story-preview request path from the CLI through committed story loading, validation, source resolution, native rendering, stale-source protection, and generated artifact writes.

sections.title: CLI
sections.body: The story preview command checks the built site, requests the committed catalogue, and later selects the requested story.

sections.title: HEAD
sections.body: Catalogue construction enumerates tracked story documents, rejects working-tree changes, and reads each document from HEAD.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body: The committed JSON is parsed against the authored story contract before its declared anchors are resolved.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.body: A stable snapshot captures every declared source path and supplies the contents used to resolve source anchors.

sections.title: Renderer
sections.body: The resolved Sequence story renders through the pinned native Archify boundary exposed by @topo/diagram-core.

sections.title: Guard
sections.body: Before publication, the catalogue verifies that captured source and repository state still match the rendered evidence.

sections.title: Writer
sections.body: The current catalogue writes generated wrappers and native viewer artifacts into the workspace site.
